items.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996
items.q: Art Dedrick, who was the founder of Kendor Music in New York, sounded me about it. He was I think the first one to start publishing for it. He was an arranger for one of the radio stations in Buffalo. And he sounded me about it and I got involved with that

ctx.x: Well originally I was writing and got calls to write for different, I wrote for Artie Shaw, it was called the “Million Dollar Band.” And that was quite an experience. Because I didn’t write the way the musicians were used to hearing it, and it wasn’t like Basie where everybody played together you know. It had individual parts. One piece was called the “Growth of an Idea” and there were seven different lines you know, so everybody in the band had to play. And unfortunately in big bands there is always a bunch of…

how to cope with it better, realistically, in terms of what people could do. And then I got into writing for jazz education. Art Dedrick, who was the founder of Kendor Music in New York, sounded me about it. He was I think the first one to start publishing for it. He was an arranger for one of the radio stations in Buffalo. And he sounded me about it and I got involved with that and then later on I was doing some for Marshall Brown and then for Berklee a great deal once I went there. In fact I was working on a…
That sounds like a big project.
